newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen positive, boosted by SAP, Siemens.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen positive, boosted by SAP, Siemens.

text.p: German shares were seen well-supported on Tuesday as Monday's losses were viewed as overdone and dealers said market tension over an expected increase in U.S. interest rates was easing.

Traders also said it appeared that the German market was benefiting from uncertainty caused by France's move towards early elections, with some investors apparently shifting funds out of French stocks into the DAX. The IBIS-DAX index of electronic trade gained a modest 15.07 points to 3,343.48 in early dealings, with June DAX futures rising 8.5 points to 3,346.5.

"The German market at the moment is not following the Dow as automatically as it often does," said one dealer, adding that investors were increasingly focussing on the early recovery potential of German stocks.
Earnings strength was visible in the first quarter results of software group SAP, which reported a 54 percent jump in pre-tax profits to 181 million on sales of just over one billion marks.
Its preference shares leapt 12.90 marks, over four percent, to 304.0 as the figures beat market expectations of pre-tax profit of just 155 million marks on 920 million of sales.
Siemens continued its recent rally ahead of Wednesday's first-half earnings report, up 1.80 marks to 91.80 on the day's best volume.
Engineering group Mannesmann also gained after it detailed its 1996 results, rising 13..50 marks to 656.0.
It earlier said group income from ordinary activities rose to 1.01 billion marks from 911 million marks, although net profit declined to 603 million marks from 701 million.
